title: Reimplementing Standard Library Utilities
pattern: Writing custom algorithms or utility procedures to perform basic, common tasks (e.g., string manipulation, command-line parsing, file operations) that are already solved by the language standard library.
why_bad: It wastes precious development time, introduces untested code paths, increases maintenance surface area, and misses optimized standard library implementations.
detection: Routines executing custom loops, string character comparisons, or file parsing logic that mirror standard library methods (e.g. `.trim()`).
counterexample: Implementing custom parsing where standard library parser utilities are insufficient for complex performance constraints.
fix: Remove the custom routine and replace it with direct calls to standard library methods.
